module_title: Acidity of Phenols, Lucas Test & Region-Selective Alkene Hydration (Intermediate)
introduction: This intermediate tier focuses on the quantitative differences in acidic behavior between alcohols and phenols, details laboratory tests used to differentiate alcohol degrees, and explores regioselective methods for converting alkenes into alcohols.

core_concepts.title: The Acidity of Phenols vs. Alcohols
core_concepts.description:
Phenol is significantly more acidic than aliphatic alcohols ($pK_a \approx 10$ vs. $16-18$). 
Reason: Phenoxide ion ($Ph-O^-$), formed after losing a proton, is highly stabilized by resonance because the negative charge is delocalized into the benzene ring. Conversely, the alkoxide ion ($R-O^-$) is destabilized by the electron-donating (+I) effect of the alkyl group, which concentrates the negative charge on a single oxygen atom. Electron Withdrawing Groups (like $-NO_2$) at ortho/para positions heavily increase phenol acidity.

core_concepts.title: The Lucas Test
core_concepts.description:
Used to distinguish between $1^\circ, 2^\circ,$ and $3^\circ$ alcohols. The reagent is a mixture of concentrated $HCl$ and anhydrous $ZnCl_2$. It proceeds via an $S_N1$ mechanism, converting soluble alcohols into insoluble alkyl chlorides, creating turbidity.
- $3^\circ$ Alcohols: Form turbidity IMMEDIATELY because their tertiary carbocation intermediate is highly stable.
- $2^\circ$ Alcohols: Form turbidity within 5 minutes.
- $1^\circ$ Alcohols: Do not produce turbidity at room temperature; requires heating.

core_concepts.title: Hydroboration-Oxidation (HBO) vs. Oxymercuration-Demercuration (OMDM)
core_concepts.description:
Two competing intermediate methods to hydrate unsymmetrical alkenes without skeletal rearrangement:
1. Hydroboration-Oxidation ($B_2H_6 / THF$ followed by $H_2O_2 / OH^-$): Results cleanly in **Anti-Markovnikov addition** of water via a syn-addition pathway. Propene yields 1-Propanol.
2. Oxymercuration-Demercuration ($Hg(OAc)_2 / H_2O$ followed by $NaBH_4$): Results cleanly in **Markovnikov addition** of water without carbocation rearrangements. Propene yields 2-Propanol.

core_concepts.title: Esterification and Acetylation
core_concepts.description: Alcohols and phenols react with carboxylic acids, acid chlorides, or acid anhydrides in the presence of an acid catalyst to form Esters. Acetylation of Salicylic Acid with acetic anhydride yields Acetylsalicylic Acid, famously known as **Aspirin** (an important analgesic and antipyretic drug).

important_entities.name: Picric Acid ($2,4,6\text{-Trinitrophenol}$)
important_entities.key_fact: An exceptionally strong organic acid that lacks a carboxyl group.
important_entities.significance: Due to the presence of three strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups ($-NO_2$) at the ortho and para positions, electron density is pulled away from the oxygen atom. The resulting conjugate base is stabilized by extensive resonance. It is so strong that its $pK_a$ mimics inorganic mineral acids, and it easily decomposes carbonates.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Alkene Acid-Catalyzed Hydration Rearragement Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If you hydrate 3,3-dimethyl-1-butene using dilute $H_2SO_4$, you might predict 3,3-dimethyl-2-butanol as the major product based on Markovnikov's rule. This is a trap. Direct acid-catalyzed hydration proceeds via a free carbocation intermediate. The initial secondary carbocation undergoes a **1,2-methyl shift** to form a more stable tertiary carbocation. The actual major product is 2,3-dimethyl-2-butanol. To bypass rearrangements and get the simple Markovnikov product, you must use OMDM instead.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the three letters: **H**ydro**B**oration **O**xidation gives an **Anti**-Markovnikov product, but the mechanistic delivery of the $-H$ and $-OH$ groups happens from the same face of the alkene (**Syn**-addition).

exam_strategy_tips: When evaluating phenol acidity with substituents: Nitro groups ($-NO_2$) increase acidity significantly more at the Para position than the Meta position. This is because the resonance (-M) effect operates only at the Ortho and Para positions, whereas the Meta position experiences only the weaker inductive (-I) effect.
